correctness.rationale: The full proof identifies suffix vertices and the unique Gaussian-exposed index exactly with the minimum of a nonstationary Gaussian random walk; disjoint left and right increments factor its angular mass. The exact Brownian variance clock proves the linear and logarithmic arcsine limits, with uniform clock convergence and uniqueness of Brownian minimizer. For square-summable weights a tail zero-one symmetry argument proves infinite sign changes and attainment of a finite unique index. The positive endpoint mass follows from an independent finite-prefix/tail maximal event. Direct objective-vs-vertex checks, exact dimension-two Gaussian orthant comparison, discrete Sparre Andersen formula and reproducible finite simulations corroborate, without substituting for proof. Boundaries n≥2 and all real alpha fixed are explicit.

value.rationale: Spherical normal-cone angles are a natural Euclidean invariant not fixed by a simplex face lattice or lattice Ehrhart data. The theorem computes every finite-dimensional angle through one-sided Gaussian persistence and identifies a sharp phase transition in the entire angular vertex-rank distribution: linear index, logarithmic index, and almost-sure finite-index concentration. The precise exponent threshold and full limiting CDF distinguish metric realizations with identical combinatorial structure. This is more than a renaming or single low-dimensional table, while making no claim that Brownian arcsine itself is new.
